title: With EMAIL_DRIVER=console in production nothing is delivered AND the body is withheld — password reset, email verification and staff invites are dead ends, and the runbook says the opposite
what: ConsoleEmailDriver computes `isDev = (process.env.NODE_ENV ?? 'development') === 'development'`. Both apps/api/Dockerfile:83 and infra/compose/docker-compose.prod.yml:35,240 set NODE_ENV=production, so the driver takes the `else` branch and logs only `NOT delivering "<subject>" to <addr> (body withheld)`. No mail is sent and no token appears anywhere an operator would look. Three user-facing flows then have no completion path: (a) POST /auth/password-reset/request mints a token into Redis and enqueues the link (apps/api/src/auth/password-reset.service.ts:70-105) — the user never receives it and there is NO admin endpoint that can reset a tenant user's password (grep of apps/api/src/admin and apps/api/src/platform for `passwordHash` returns only the admin's own login check, admin-auth.service.ts:39); (b) email verification never arrives, so `users.emailVerifiedAt` stays NULL forever; (c) EmailVerifiedGuard (apps/api/src/auth/email-verified.guard.ts:37) is applied to POST /t/:slug/staff (apps/api/src/staff/staff.controller.ts:51), so the owner can never add a second librarian. The only recovery is an undocumented `select "bodyMarkdown" from email_outbox` in psql, inside the token's 60-minute TTL. docs/deploy-from-the-server.md:113 tells the operator the opposite — that the console driver 'writes password-reset links into `docker logs api`' — which is true only in development.
impact: On day one a librarian who forgets their password is locked out of their library permanently unless the sole operator SSHes in and runs a psql query nobody has written down, within 60 minutes of the request. A library that hires a second member of staff cannot add them at all. The one document an operator would consult during that incident gives an instruction that does not work.
evidence: READ console-driver.ts:21 `private readonly isDev = (process.env.NODE_ENV ?? 'development') === 'development';` and :33 `console driver in a non-dev environment: NOT delivering ... (body withheld)`. READ Dockerfile:83 `ENV NODE_ENV=production`. EXECUTED against the live audit environment (integration probe, signup then POST /t/<slug>/staff): `### SIGNUP 201`, `### INVITE STAFF 403 {"code":"email_verification_required",...}`, `### OWNER emailVerifiedAt = null`, and the outbox showed `{"kind":"email_verification","to":"owner@lrp-6e683b.test","status":"pending"}`. EXECUTED `psql \d email_outbox` — `bodyMarkdown text not null` confirms the psql escape hatch exists but is undocumented.
fix: Do not go public on console. Either (a) provision Resend, set EMAIL_DRIVER=resend + EMAIL_FROM and the DNS in finding 03, or (b) if launching on console anyway: add an owner-only admin endpoint that force-verifies a tenant user's email and issues a one-time password-reset link returned in the HTTP response, add an 'Emails' page to the admin panel that renders the outbox body, and correct docs/deploy-from-the-server.md:113 to say the body is withheld in production and where the link actually lives.

title: The launch offer is not mechanically deliverable: putting a tenant on Municipal forces billingMode=stripe, and set-paid-until then refuses — the documented founding-library procedure returns 400
what: docs/billing-go-live.md:115 states the go-live precondition: "Founding-offer libraries must be on `billingMode = 'manual'` with `paidUntil` twelve months out before this flips, or they get charged for what they were promised free." That state cannot be reached. `applyAdminPlanChange` writes `billingMode: plan.billingMode` (billing.service.ts:414) — denormalised from the plan — and every sellable plan is seeded `stripe`; only `on-prem-enterprise` is `manual`. `applyManualPayment` then hard-refuses: `if (sub.billingMode !== 'manual') throw new BadRequestException('Manual paid-until only applies to manually-billed plans...')` (billing.service.ts:452-456). There is no admin endpoint that sets `subscription.billingMode` independently of the plan. Consequently a founding library placed on Municipal sits at `billingMode=stripe, status=active, stripeSubscriptionId=null, paidUntil=null`, and EffectivePlanService's join (effective-plan.service.ts:180) only expires `manual` subscriptions — so the twelve months have no end date and nothing in the system will ever end them.
impact: Two failure modes, both commercial. Before billing is switched on the five founding libraries can only be granted Municipal by leaving them in a state the go-live runbook explicitly forbids; when BILLING_ENABLED flips they either get gated wrongly or stay free forever with no expiry and no dunning. The offer terms promise 'the account simply stops being active' at month thirteen (apps/site/content/programme-terms.en.md) — no code path produces that outcome.
evidence: EXECUTED against the live audit environment via the admin API: `### SET-PLAN municipal 201 {"tenantId":"cmt5n37xm...","billingMode":"stripe","status":"active","plan":{"slug":"municipal"},"paidUntil":null,...}` then `### SET-PAID-UNTIL 400 {"message":"Manual paid-until only applies to manually-billed plans. Use Stripe for stripe-billed tenants.","statusCode":400}`. EXECUTED `psql -c 'select slug, "billingMode" from plans'` → starter/community/municipal/central/institutional all `stripe`; only `on-prem-enterprise` is `manual`.
fix: Add an owner-only admin action that sets `subscription.billingMode='manual'` together with `paidUntil` (one endpoint, audited), or seed a dedicated `founding-municipal` plan with `billingMode='manual'` and the Municipal feature values and place the five libraries on it. Then walk one tenant through the full path — set plan, set paidUntil 12 months out, flip BILLING_ENABLED=true, confirm features stay on and confirm they drop the day after paidUntil — before any library is told they have a place.

title: The commercial funnel has no notification and no admin screen: an application lands in Postgres and nobody is told, while the site promises an answer within two working days
what: `ApplicationsService.notify` enqueues an `application_submitted` email to `applyNotifyTo` (info@libriant.com). That enqueue goes through the same EmailService as everything else, so under EMAIL_DRIVER=console it is logged-and-dropped (see finding 01). There is no fallback channel — no webhook, no Slack, no admin badge. On the read side the admin panel has no Applications page: the directory listing of apps/web/app/[locale]/admin/(authed)/ contains announcements, export, fleet, library-requests, maintenance, mfa, plans, subscriptions, support, system-mode, tenants — and nothing for applications; AdminSidebar.tsx:32-42 lists the same eleven items. The only read path is a bare CSV route, `GET /admin/applications.csv` (apps/api/src/applications/applications.controller.ts:113), which is not linked from anywhere in the UI.
impact: The launch campaign drives 277 mailboxes to a form whose submissions are invisible. apps/site/content/pages.en.json (/en/contact, /en/faq) promises 'We answer every application within two working days, yes or no' and 'No question is left unanswered on purpose'. The first five founding places are awarded 'in order of application' — an order nobody can observe. Leads are not lost (the row commits) but they are silently unread until someone thinks to type a URL that appears in no menu.
evidence: READ applications.service.ts:169-186 — the notification is `this.email.enqueue({ kind: 'application_submitted', toEmail: this.notifyTo, ... })`, the only delivery mechanism. EXECUTED `ls 'apps/web/app/[locale]/admin/(authed)/'` → no `applications` directory. READ AdminSidebar.tsx:32-42 — eleven nav entries, none for applications. READ pages.en.json /en/contact: 'We answer every message within two working days.'
fix: Before the campaign sends: add an Applications page to the admin panel (list + status + the CSV as a download button), and give the notification a delivery path that does not depend on the mail driver — at minimum a startup-time refusal to run with `EMAIL_DRIVER=console` while `spotsRemaining > 0`, at best a real mailbox via finding 04.

title: The DNS is not prepared for transactional email: SPF authorises only iCloud, there is no DMARC record, and the sending domain is the same one the campaign mails from
what: The product's default sender is `Libriant <no-reply@${PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN}>` (env.ts:387-390) i.e. no-reply@libriant.com, and site.config.json declares `notifyFrom: no-reply@libriant.com`. Live DNS today publishes `v=spf1 include:icloud.com ~all` and no `_dmarc` TXT record at all. Switching EMAIL_DRIVER to `resend` (the documented next step, docs/deploy-from-the-server.md:112) would send from an IP that SPF does not authorise, with no DKIM selector for the provider and no DMARC policy or reporting. This is not covered by 'no Resend key yet' — the key is one step; the DNS is a separate, unstarted one, and Resend also requires domain verification records before it will send at all.
impact: The first real emails Libriant sends — password resets, verification links, member overdue notices, and the 277-mailbox launch campaign — go out unauthenticated from a domain with no DMARC. Greek municipal and academic mail systems junk or reject that. The failure is invisible from the sending side: the outbox rows read `delivered`. A password-reset link that lands in a spam folder is indistinguishable, to the librarian, from the outage in finding 01.
evidence: EXECUTED `dig +short libriant.com TXT` → `"v=spf1 include:icloud.com ~all"` and `"apple-domain=KbpauxgxXHf5ijQq"`. EXECUTED `dig +short _dmarc.libriant.com TXT` → empty. EXECUTED `dig +short libriant.com MX` → `mx01/mx02.mail.icloud.com`. READ env.ts:387-390 for the default From.
fix: Before enabling any real driver: add the provider to SPF (`include:` alongside icloud.com), publish the provider's DKIM CNAMEs, and publish `_dmarc.libriant.com` starting at `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:...` so failures are visible, tightening to quarantine once the reports are clean. Verify with a seed send to a Gmail and an Outlook address and read the Authentication-Results header. Do this before the campaign, not after.

title: 'Daily backups with an off-server copy' is asserted in the offer terms and on the site, but nothing installs the cron, no offsite target exists, and no alert fires when either is missing
where: scripts/backup.sh:185-201; scripts/deploy-on-host.sh (no cron step); docs/deployment-hetzner.md:645; apps/site/content/programme-terms.en.md
what: Three separate gaps behind one published claim. (1) The nightly job is installed only by a hand-run `sudo tee /etc/cron.d/libriant-backup` in docs/deployment-hetzner.md:645. `scripts/deploy-on-host.sh` checks for docker, the data directories, the origin certificate and the admin email, but never checks that the backup cron exists — a completely green first deploy has zero backups and says nothing about it. (2) Offsite requires `RCLONE_REMOTE`, which `scripts/ensure-env.sh` does not default and .env.prod.example:101 ships empty; with it unset backup.sh:200 logs `WARN: RCLONE_REMOTE unset — NO OFF-SITE COPY` to a file. (3) `BACKUP_HEARTBEAT_URL` (backup.sh:206) — the only dead-man's switch — is not in .env.prod.example at all, so it will not be set by accident. Combined with finding 06 there is no alert destination, so all three warnings land in `/var/log/libriant/backup.log` and nowhere else.
impact: apps/site/content/programme-terms.en.md tells the first five libraries in writing: 'Your data is hosted in the European Union, with daily backups and an off-server copy.' /en/faq repeats 'with daily backups and a copy kept off the server.' On the box as the runbook actually leaves it, both halves of that sentence are false by default and stay false silently. The handbook is explicit that on a dedicated box 'backups are the only recovery option' (§8) — so the gap between the claim and the machine is the gap between a recoverable incident and a lost catalogue.
evidence: READ deploy-on-host.sh in full — preconditions at lines 46-77 cover docker/data dirs/origin cert/admin email; there is no reference to cron, backup.sh or BACKUP_ROOT anywhere in the script. READ deployment-hetzner.md:645 — the cron is a manual `sudo tee`. READ backup.sh:198-201 and :206-211. READ .env.prod.example — `RCLONE_REMOTE=` (line 101) blank; `grep -n HEARTBEAT .env.prod.example` returns nothing. READ ensure-env.sh — neither key appears in its ensure_default list.
fix: Add a precondition to deploy-on-host.sh that fails the deploy when /etc/cron.d/libriant-backup is absent or when the newest directory under $BACKUP_ROOT is older than 48h. Provision the Hetzner Storage Box and set RCLONE_REMOTE, or amend the site and the offer terms to drop 'off-server copy' until it exists. Add BACKUP_HEARTBEAT_URL to .env.prod.example and point it at a free healthchecks.io check — that one line is the difference between noticing a stopped backup tomorrow and noticing it in six months.

title: Nothing tells anyone when it breaks: no Alertmanager, no uptime monitor, no on-call — the shipped alert rules fire into a dashboard that is not running
what: The monitoring stack is real (Prometheus 3.1.0, node-exporter, cAdvisor, Grafana) and the rules cover the right things, but the Alertmanager block in prometheus.yml:19-21 is commented out and no Alertmanager service exists in infra/monitoring/docker-compose.monitoring.yml. The handbook admits this at :389 — 'Prometheus does not deliver alerts by itself... the rules fire into a dashboard nobody is looking at. Until you configure that, treat the weekly sweep as your alerting system.' Separately, `scripts/deploy-on-host.sh` never starts the monitoring compose file, so on a fresh box even the dashboard is absent unless the operator runs it by hand. docs/cutover-three-hosts.md Step 7 says 'Repoint uptime monitors' — there is no evidence any uptime monitor exists; libriant.com/healthz has had no origin behind it since 2026-08-22 and nothing in the repo or docs names a monitoring provider or an on-call address.
impact: The detection time for any outage is 'until the sole operator next looks', which the handbook sets at weekly. That is the same class of failure as the DR restore that was broken for months: a silent condition with no observer. A library that opens on Monday to a 502 has no way to report it except an email address that, per finding 01, the operator may also not be receiving.
evidence: READ prometheus.yml:19-21 — the alertmanagers stanza is inside a comment block. EXECUTED `grep -rn alertmanager infra/monitoring/` — only those commented lines; no service, no config. READ server-handbook.md:389. READ deploy-on-host.sh — no reference to infra/monitoring. EXECUTED `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://libriant.com/` → timed out after 8s (no origin), so any monitor that did exist has been alerting or silent for a day and nothing in the repo records which.
fix: Before DNS is pointed at the box: (1) add Alertmanager to infra/monitoring/docker-compose.monitoring.yml with a route to a real destination the operator reads on a phone (email to a non-libriant.com address, or a push service — not an address that depends on the system being up); (2) add the two hardware alerts the handbook already names as missing (node_md_disks failed, NVMe percentage_used); (3) create external uptime checks on https://libriant.com/healthz and https://app.libriant.com/healthz with a third-party provider so an origin-down condition is detected from outside; (4) start the monitoring stack from deploy-on-host.sh, or check for it and refuse.

title: Public legal pages render the author's internal drafting note to visitors: the DPA opens with 'Replace every [PLACEHOLDER] and have it reviewed before you rely on it'
where: apps/web/lib/legal.ts:81; locales/en/legal/dpa.md:1-3 (and terms, privacy, cookies, acceptable-use, legal-notice, el/*)
what: That the legal documents are drafts is known. What is not is that the drafting instruction is inside the shipped markdown and is rendered verbatim to the public. `loadLegalDoc` does `marked.parse(raw)` on the whole file (legal.ts:81) with no front-matter or banner stripping, and the page injects the result (apps/web/app/[locale]/legal/[doc]/page.tsx:48). dpa.md lines 1-3 are a blockquote reading '> **Draft — pending review by qualified legal counsel.** This document is a tailored starting point, not legal advice. Replace every `[PLACEHOLDER]` and have it reviewed before you rely on it.' — so a visitor sees that above the app's own draft Banner. Unfilled bracket values render literally too: legal-notice.md shows '[e.g. Private Company (IKE) / S.A. (AE)]', terms.md shows '[exclusive/inclusive]' and '[via email at [CONTACT EMAIL]'. The route needs no auth (page.tsx:11 comment) and infra/caddy/Caddyfile redirects libriant.com/en/legal/* and /el/legal/* straight to it, so the marketing site actively sends visitors there.
impact: The audience for these pages is a municipal IT department, a bursar or a school's legal reviewer — the site says so explicitly and tells librarians to forward them. What they will read at the top of the Data Processing Agreement is an instruction to the author to fill in the blanks. Worse, apps/site/content/pages.en.json (/en/security) tells them 'The text is not published yet: it is with legal review and will be provided when it is ready' — while the same domain redirects them to the published draft. That contradiction, discovered by the reader, costs the deal.
evidence: READ legal.ts:78-83 — `const html = await marked.parse(raw, { async: true });` with `raw` the unmodified file. READ page.tsx:44-50 — `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: rendered.html }}`. EXECUTED `head -8 locales/en/legal/dpa.md` → the drafting blockquote is lines 1-3. EXECUTED `grep -o "\[[a-z][^]]*\]" locales/en/legal/*.md` → `[once per year]`, `[e.g. Private Company (IKE) / S.A. (AE)]`, `[exclusive/inclusive]`, `[via email at [CONTACT EMAIL]`. READ Caddyfile — `@moved path ... /el/legal/* /en/legal/*` → `redir ... https://app.libriant.com{uri} 302`.
fix: Strip the leading drafting blockquote in loadLegalDoc (drop a leading `> **Draft` block) so the internal note can never render, and fill or remove the bracketed values. Then decide one story and make both surfaces tell it: either publish the DPA and change /en/security's 'not published yet' sentence, or 404 the /legal/dpa route until counsel has signed off and drop the Caddy redirect for it.

title: admin.libriant.com is already live in DNS pointing at a released IP, and neither cutover document knows the record exists
what: Both documents inventory DNS as 'libriant.com resolves to Cloudflare with no origin, app.libriant.com has no A record' and instruct the operator to add only the `app` record at Step 2. That inventory is incomplete: `admin.libriant.com` already resolves, proxied through Cloudflare, and hangs — its origin is the decommissioned 178.104.32.176, an address Hetzner has taken back and will reassign. Step 2's guidance ('No new certificate is needed... verify before proceeding') is written for a record being created, not for one that already exists and points somewhere wrong. Nothing in the cutover sequence repoints or deletes it.
impact: Two things. Operationally, an operator following cutover-three-hosts.md end to end deploys the box, adds `app`, verifies TLS, and never touches `admin` — which then continues to proxy to whoever now holds 178.104.32.176. If Cloudflare's SSL/TLS mode is anything other than Full (strict), admin.libriant.com — the host that serves the admin login — proxies to a stranger's server on a hostname covered by the origin certificate and by HSTS includeSubDomains. Commercially, a prospect who tries the admin host today gets an 8-second hang rather than a page.
evidence: EXECUTED `dig +short admin.libriant.com A` → `172.67.218.62`, `104.21.83.86` (Cloudflare). EXECUTED `dig +short app.libriant.com A` → empty. EXECUTED `dig +short www.libriant.com A` → empty. EXECUTED `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 8 https://admin.libriant.com/` → `curl: (28) Operation timed out`. READ cutover-three-hosts.md:82-88 — the measured DNS block lists only libriant.com, app.libriant.com and the dead box; admin.libriant.com is absent.
fix: Add the real, current DNS inventory to cutover-three-hosts.md Step 1 (it should be re-derived with dig at cutover time, not quoted from August). Repoint admin.libriant.com to 195.201.13.95 in the same change as the app record, and confirm Cloudflare SSL/TLS mode is Full (strict) before either goes live — that setting is the only thing standing between a stale record and a reassigned IP.

title: The offer terms tell the first five libraries the system 'passed a full security audit', which is not what happened
what: programme-terms.en.md states, as a term of the offer: 'The system **passed a full security audit** before release and is covered by automated tests that run on every change to the code.' The site's own /en/security page contradicts this and is the accurate one: 'It was an internal review, not certification by an independent body, and we do not present it as one.' The only review on record is docs/audit/preprod-final-2026-06-21, a self-audit which certified this codebase as ready while the disaster-recovery restore path had never once worked — a defect found two months later on 2026-08-22 and fixed only then. This audit, run today, is producing further blockers.
impact: The offer terms are the document a school bursar or a municipal committee files. 'Passed a full security audit' reads to that reader as an external assessment. It is a claim that cannot be substantiated if asked for the report, and the honest version already exists 300 metres away on the same site — which makes the discrepancy look like the terms were written to close rather than to inform. The site's whole positioning rests on 'we tell you what we do not have'; this is the one sentence that breaks it.
evidence: READ programme-terms.en.md, section 'Security and availability', first bullet. READ pages.en.json /en/security, section 'A security review before release': 'The system went through a systematic security and reliability review... It was an internal review, not certification by an independent body, and we do not present it as one.' The brief for this audit states docs/audit/preprod-final-2026-06-21 'certified this codebase as ready. The DR restore was broken the entire time and had never once worked.'
fix: Rewrite the bullet to match /en/security — 'went through an internal security and reliability review before release; not an independent certification' — and add the automated-test sentence separately, which is true (verify.yml runs unit + integration + dr:drill on every push). Changing marketing copy is a commit and a full deploy (docs/cutover-three-hosts.md, 'What changed operationally'), so make this edit before the site is first published, not after.

title: The site advertises prices for plans that cannot lawfully be sold: the business is not registered, and the build lints Greek copy to hide it
what: apps/site/build.ts carries an error-level copy lint that fails the build if the Greek pages contain «εταιρεία», «ΓΕΜΗ», «ΑΦΜ», «ΦΠΑ», «τιμολόγιο» or «τιμολογούμε», with the stated reason 'The business is not registered and nothing is trademarked.' The same site publishes a five-tier price list (€390/€790/€1,190/€1,890 annually) and the offer terms promise 'Before any charge you will receive full commercial and pricing details, along with the service agreement.' In Greece a charge requires a registered entity with a ΑΦΜ that can issue a compliant invoice; Stripe also requires a legal entity for a live account. So the entire paid path — the one docs/billing-go-live.md describes in operational detail — is blocked on something outside the codebase and not tracked anywhere in it.
impact: The twelve free months are deliverable precisely because no money moves; month thirteen is not, and nothing in the launch plan schedules the company registration that unblocks it. Meanwhile the pricing page invites a municipal finance office to budget against figures nobody can currently invoice. If a library says yes in month eleven, the entity, the Stripe account, the eight real Prices and the VAT treatment all have to exist by then — a multi-week external process, started from zero.
evidence: READ build.ts:177-182 — `name: 'company-language', level: 'error', re: /εταιρ[εί]α|ΓΕΜΗ|ΑΦΜ|ΦΠΑ|™|®|.../, why: 'The business is not registered and nothing is trademarked.'` READ pages.en.json /en/pricing — the four annual figures. EXECUTED `psql -c 'select slug, "stripePriceId" from plans'` → every id is a `price_seed_*` placeholder, confirming no Stripe Product exists either.
fix: Put the entity registration on the launch timeline with a date, working back from month eleven of the first founding library, and record it in docs/billing-go-live.md as step zero — above 'Create the Prices in Stripe', which cannot happen without it. Until then the pricing page is a statement of intent; say so, or accept that the first renewal conversation starts with a company that does not exist yet.

title: 'Five places, given in order of application' is a hand-maintained JSON literal that requires a full CI run and a manual deploy to change, and is wired to nothing
what: `offer.spotsRemaining` is a constant in site.config.json. It gates the public form server-side (applications.controller.ts:51: `if (config.offer.spotsRemaining <= 0) redirect`) and is rendered as a scarcity counter on the home page (apps/site/src/pages.ts:246). Nothing decrements it: it is not derived from the `applications` table, not from the count of provisioned tenants, and not from any admin action. Changing it is a commit, a full verify run and a manual on-box deploy — docs/cutover-three-hosts.md says so explicitly ('`offer.spotsRemaining` is a commit too... It is now a full CI run'). Separately, tenant signup at app.libriant.com/signup is fully self-serve with no closed-registration switch anywhere in the platform settings, so the pool of libraries in the system is unrelated to the pool of applications.
impact: The number on the home page is a claim made to every visitor and will be wrong within days of the campaign — either stale-high (advertising places already promised, so the sixth applicant is told no after being told five remained) or stale-low. Because closing the offer is also a deploy, the form cannot be shut quickly: if all five go in one morning, the sixth through twentieth applications are accepted by a form that should have closed.
evidence: READ site.config.json:16 `"spotsRemaining": 5`. READ applications.controller.ts:48-53 — the gate reads the compiled constant. EXECUTED `grep -rn spotsRemaining apps/ scripts/` — five call sites, all reads; no writer. EXECUTED `grep -rn 'signupsEnabled|SIGNUP_ENABLED|signup_enabled' apps/api/src` → no matches; there is no way to close registration.
fix: Move the counter behind the platform-settings table (the same mechanism as billing.enabled, which already has an admin UI and cache invalidation) so closing the offer is a click, and have the marketing page read it at request time via the /apply host rather than baking it into a static build. Failing that, decide before launch who checks the applications table daily and how fast a deploy can close the form, and write that number down.

title: There is no customer-facing incident procedure: the handbook's 'When it breaks' never says tell the libraries, and the DPA commits to breach notification with no path to deliver it
what: Part 9 is a competent infrastructure runbook — symptom-indexed, honest about ordering, correct about not rebooting a degraded array. It is silent on every customer-facing action. It never mentions the product's own incident tooling: MAINTENANCE_HARD (documented only in deployment-hetzner.md:762), the `system-mode` states (maintenance / read_only / out_of_order / under_construction, schema.prisma:159-165) or the announcements feature that pushes a banner to tenants. It contains no template for what to say, no decision on when to say it, and no list of who to say it to. Meanwhile locales/en/legal/dpa.md:110-114 commits: 'We will notify you **without undue delay** after becoming aware of a personal-data breach affecting Controller Personal Data' — a GDPR Art. 33(2) processor obligation whose only delivery channel is email, which does not work (finding 01), to a contact list that exists only as rows in the tenants table.
impact: The first customer-visible incident will be improvised by one person at an inconvenient hour, deciding in the moment whether to flip maintenance mode, whether to post an announcement, and how to reach five libraries. For a personal-data breach that improvisation is a compliance failure with a clock on it: 'without undue delay' is measured from awareness, and the notification path has to be established before it is needed, not during.
evidence: READ server-handbook.md Part 9 in full — 9.1 through 9.9 cover down/disk/OOM/CPU/RAID/postgres/TLS/firewall/bad-deploy; `grep -n 'announcement|system-mode|MAINTENANCE_HARD|status page' docs/server-handbook.md` returns nothing. READ dpa.md:110-114. READ schema.prisma:159-165 for the SystemModeKind enum the runbook does not mention.
fix: Add a Part 9.0 to the handbook: the three customer-facing levers in order of severity (announcement banner → system-mode read_only/maintenance → MAINTENANCE_HARD at the edge), who to tell and on what channel, and a two-paragraph holding statement to fill in. Add a separate short breach-notification checklist keyed to the DPA's own wording, including where the five libraries' contact addresses live and a channel that does not depend on the app being up.

title: The single admin account has TOTP mandatory in production, no recovery codes, and no second admin — losing the phone locks the operator out of the admin panel entirely
what: `adminMfaRequired` defaults to `!isDev` (env.ts:311), so in production the bootstrapped admin is forced into MFA enrollment before anything else (admin-auth.guard.ts:65). Enrollment works — /admin/mfa/setup and /verify exist (apps/api/src/support/mfa.controller.ts:26-29) with a UI at apps/web/app/[locale]/admin/(authed)/mfa. But the AdminUser model has no recovery-code field (schema.prisma:805-835: passwordHash, mfaSecretCipher, mfaNonce, mfaKeyId, mfaEnabled — nothing else), `/admin/mfa/disable` is itself behind an authenticated admin session, and the TOTP secret is encrypted under MFA_MASTER_KEY, which ensure-env.sh mints per host and which lives only in the password manager (backups exclude .env.prod by design). scripts/bootstrap-admin.ts is the only way to create an admin and it is a shell command on the box; it does not enroll MFA.
impact: A lost or wiped phone locks the sole operator out of admin.libriant.com — which is where library edit-requests are approved, plans are set, billing is flipped, support access is granted and the applications CSV is served. Recovery is SSH plus a hand-written UPDATE against admin_users. If MFA_MASTER_KEY is lost as well (it is in exactly one place, and by design not in any backup), every enrolled secret becomes undecryptable. This is the same single-point-of-failure shape the handbook already warns about for SSH keys ('keep at least two keys authorized') and does not apply to the admin login.
evidence: READ env.ts:311 `adminMfaRequired: bool('ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED', !isDev)`. READ admin-auth.guard.ts:65 — 403 `mfa_enrollment_required` for any non-/mfa/ non-/auth/ path. EXECUTED `grep -rn 'recovery|backupCode|recoveryCode' apps/api/src/support/mfa.service.ts apps/api/src/support/mfa.controller.ts packages/db-control/prisma/schema.prisma` → one unrelated comment, no field, no endpoint. READ schema.prisma:805-835 for the full AdminUser model. READ ensure-env.sh — `ensure_rand MFA_MASTER_KEY 32`.
fix: Before the box goes into DNS: bootstrap a second owner admin on a separate device and enroll it, and store both TOTP seeds in the password manager alongside MFA_MASTER_KEY. Add the recovery procedure (the exact SQL, and the fact that MFA_MASTER_KEY is required to decrypt an existing secret) to server-handbook.md Part 10 as a numbered procedure — it belongs next to 10.3 Rotate a secret.

title: The container's pg_dump major version floats while the server is pinned at 16 — the exported SQL dump may not restore where the site promises it will
what: The api/worker image does `RUN apk add --no-cache openssl tini postgresql-client` (Dockerfile:22) with no version pin, so the pg_dump major is whatever the current node:26-alpine base's Alpine release defaults to (17 or 18 today, rising with each base bump), while the server is deliberately held at postgres:16-alpine. Dumping an older server with a newer client is supported, but the emitted header carries the client's settings: a pg_dump 18 dump opens with `SET transaction_timeout = 0;`, a parameter PostgreSQL 16 and earlier do not recognise, and psql aborts on it. docs/server-handbook.md §8 records this exact failure measured against this cluster ('dumping 16 with the 18 client produces SET transaction_timeout = 0;, and the restore aborts'), for backups — the same hazard applies to the customer-facing export and is not mentioned anywhere near it. The dump also emits `\restrict`/`\unrestrict` meta-commands that only recent psql builds understand.
impact: The SQL export is the site's load-bearing answer to 'and what if you disappear?': '/en/about — The SQL copy does not depend on us in order to be read: it restores onto any PostgreSQL server, by any technician'; '/en/migration — a complete copy of your library's database, made with pg_dump, without owners and privileges, which restores into any PostgreSQL installation.' A library whose technician restores onto their own PostgreSQL 15 or 16 gets an error, at exactly the moment the promise is being tested. Nobody would find out before then, because nothing in CI restores an export.
evidence: READ Dockerfile:22 — unpinned `postgresql-client`. READ export-processors.ts:349-353 — `execFileP('pg_dump', ['--no-owner','--no-privileges','--format=plain','--file',outPath])`. READ server-handbook.md §8, the version-skew note. EXECUTED the export end to end against the live audit environment (processExportJob on a real tenant): `AFTER {"status":"completed","fileName":"libriant-lrp-6e683b-2026-08-23.sql","bytes":37023,"error":null}`, and the produced file restored cleanly into a fresh database (`psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f <dump>` → exit 0, 15 tables) — but with the local pg_dump 16.15, which is the version-matched case, not the container's. The dump header reads `Dumped by pg_dump version 16.15` and contains `\restrict`. Docker is not available in this environment, so the container's actual client major could not be measured.
fix: Pin the client to the server major in apps/api/Dockerfile — `apk add --no-cache postgresql16-client` — and add a CI step that takes a tenant export and restores it into a stock postgres:16 container, asserting exit 0. That test is the only thing that keeps the /en/about promise honest as base images move.

title: In-app help is four articles and is installed by a best-effort step that cannot fail a deploy — yet the site sells it as one of only four support mechanisms
what: prod-bootstrap.sh runs `pnpm ingest:help || echo '[bootstrap] help ingest skipped (non-fatal)'` — a failure is swallowed and the deploy goes green with an empty help centre. The corpus itself is four articles per language: getting-started, adding-members, lending-books, reservations. There is nothing on returning a copy, fines, importing a file, exporting data, custom fields, staff and roles, barcode scanning, the desktop app, or settings — including no article on the data export, which is the single feature the site leans on hardest.
impact: apps/site/content/pages.en.json (/en/about) lists exactly four things that stand in for a support organisation: 'two email addresses, step-by-step help inside the application, a reply to every message within two working days, and availability and support terms agreed with you in writing.' One of those four is four articles, and it can silently be zero. Every gap in it converts into an email to the one person who also writes the code — the load the help centre exists to absorb.
evidence: READ prod-bootstrap.sh:46-47. EXECUTED against the live audit environment: `psql -c 'select count(*) from help_articles'` → 0 after migrate+seed, i.e. seeding alone does not populate it; then `pnpm ingest:help` → `[help:en] upserted=4 archived=0 / [help:el] upserted=4 archived=0`; then `select locale, slug, title from help_articles` → 8 rows, the four topics above in each language. EXECUTED `ls locales/en/help/` → 01-getting-started.md, 02-adding-members.md, 03-lending-books.md, 04-reservations.md.
fix: Write the missing everyday articles before the first library is onboarded — returns, fines, import, export, staff and roles at minimum; export first, since it backs the strongest claim on the site. Make the ingest step fatal in prod-bootstrap.sh, or add a readiness check that refuses the deploy when help_articles is empty: an empty help centre is indistinguishable from a working one until a librarian goes looking.

title: The plan catalogue ships three feature flags the product does not have and the site explicitly disclaims — api_access, custom_subdomain, priority_support
what: The seeded catalogue grants `api_access_enabled: true` on Municipal, Central and Institutional; `priority_support: true` on Central and Institutional; and `custom_subdomain_enabled: true` on Institutional. All three contradict published copy. The site says there is no API in four places, including '/en/security — No. There is no programming interface, and we will not tell you otherwise in order to get through an evaluation', and apps/site/build.ts even lints the Greek phrase «πρόσβαση API» out of the copy as 'a claim the code does not support'. On support: '/en/about — we do not sell tiers of support: no plan buys a faster answer.' Custom subdomains cannot work at all — the `*.libriant.com` vhost in infra/caddy/Caddyfile is entirely commented out and needs a DNS-01 wildcard certificate that is not provisioned.
impact: Low today because the tenant-facing plan grid renders only name, description and price (apps/web/app/[locale]/t/[slug]/billing/PlanGrid.tsx has no feature matrix) and /t/:slug/plan is dev-only. The exposure is the moment anyone builds a comparison table from the catalogue, or an admin quotes the plan record to a prospect: the database says Municipal includes API access, and the website says the API does not exist. It also means an Institutional customer could be sold a custom subdomain the edge cannot serve.
evidence: EXECUTED `psql` pivot over plan_feature_values → `api_access_enabled` false/false/true/true/true, `priority_support` false/false/false/true/true, `custom_subdomain_enabled` false/false/false/false/true across starter→institutional. READ seed-data.ts:97-99 and the four sibling blocks. READ Caddyfile — the `*.{$PUBLIC_APEX_DOMAIN}` block is commented from `# *.{...} {` to the closing `# }`. READ build.ts:222-226 — the `terminology-drift` lint bans «πρόσβαση API» with `why: 'Glossary violation, or a claim the code does not support.'` EXECUTED `grep -rn 'api_access_enabled|priority_support' apps/web packages/i18n locales` → no matches, confirming nothing renders them today.
fix: Set all three to false across every plan in seed-data.ts until the features exist, or delete the feature keys. A catalogue that disagrees with the website is a claim waiting for a UI to surface it.

title: A tenant cannot see its own usage against its plan limits in production, so the first signal a library gets when billing turns on is the refusal itself
what: `GET /t/:slug/plan` and `GET /t/:slug/plan/usage` are mounted on PlanDemoController, which is gated by `NonProductionOnlyGuard` (plan-demo.controller.ts:72) — `enabled = loadEnv().nodeEnv !== 'production'`, throwing NotFoundException otherwise. The guard is correct for its purpose: the same controller carries `POST /t/:slug/demo/books`, a real unvalidated write that bypasses the race-safe quota authority, and that must not be reachable in production. But it takes the two read-only usage endpoints down with it. docs/billing-go-live.md flags the consequence ('A tenant cannot see their own usage in production') and then proceeds to the flip anyway.
impact: Once BILLING_ENABLED=true the real caps bite immediately against data loaded with none in force. A librarian mid-task meets a 402 with no screen anywhere in the product showing how many of their 60,000 titles or 25 staff seats are used. The handbook's related note that `storageUsedBytes` never self-heals (nothing schedules recomputeUsage) means a stale counter can refuse an upload that should succeed, again with no visible number to argue with.
evidence: READ plan-demo.controller.ts:44-53 (the guard) and :68-73 (`@UseGuards(NonProductionOnlyGuard, TenantGuard, RolesGuard, PlanGuard)`). EXECUTED against the live audit environment where NODE_ENV=test: `### PLAN USAGE 200` — the endpoint works and returns real counters, so only the production guard stands between a library and its own numbers. READ billing-go-live.md, 'Before you flip it' section.
fix: Split the two read-only endpoints out of PlanDemoController into a plain tenant controller behind TenantGuard/RolesGuard, leaving the demo write behind NonProductionOnlyGuard, and surface the numbers on the billing page. Do it before BILLING_ENABLED is flipped, not after the first 402.

title: What is genuinely ready — verified rather than assumed
what: Recorded so the blockers above are read in proportion, and so a later reader does not re-verify these. Each was executed, not read. (1) The test suites are green on this commit: 343 unit tests in 47 files, 53 integration tests in 10 files, all passing against the live Postgres 16 + Redis audit environment — so verify.yml, which gates the deploy job, would pass. (2) The tenant SQL export works end to end and the site's flagship claim holds: a real export produced a 37,023-byte plain dump that restored into a fresh database with `ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, exit 0, 15 tables (subject to finding 14 on client-version drift). (3) The export TTL machinery is complete — EXPORT_TTL_HOURS=24 matches the site's 'valid for 24 hours', and apps/api/src/jobs/export-cleanup.job.ts purges expired artefacts and reclaims stuck jobs. (4) The marketing site's 'no cookies, no analytics' claim is true: the built dist contains no <script> tag and no third-party asset, and the site vhost's CSP is `script-src 'none'`. (5) apps/site/dist contains no unfilled [PLACEHOLDER] or {{token}}, and build.ts enforces that plus eleven copy-lint rules at error level. (6) apps/site/dist/sw.js is a deliberate self-unregistering service worker that cleans up the old PWA scope at the apex — a real cutover hazard already handled. (7) Every long-running service in docker-compose.prod.yml (api, web, worker) declares a healthcheck, so deploy-on-host.sh's 180-second health gate can actually succeed. (8) scripts/deploy-on-host.sh checks the four data directories, the origin certificate, the git checkout, docker and the admin email before it touches anything, and validates the Caddyfile before recreating containers — the failure modes it names are the real ones. (9) The desktop app already defaults to https://app.libriant.com (apps/desktop/src/config.ts:11), so the cutover ordering warning is satisfied rather than pending.
impact: None — this is context. The gap between this repo and a live service is operational and commercial, not a codebase that does not work.
evidence: EXECUTED `pnpm --filter @libriant/api exec vitest run --project unit` → 'Test Files 47 passed (47) / Tests 343 passed (343)'. EXECUTED `... --project integration` → 'Test Files 10 passed (10) / Tests 53 passed (53)'. EXECUTED processExportJob on a real tenant → completed, 37023 bytes; then `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f <dump>` into a fresh DB → exit 0, `select count(*) from information_schema.tables where table_schema='public'` → 15. EXECUTED `grep -n 'cookie|gtag|analytics|<script' apps/site/dist/index.html` → one Greek prose line claiming no tracking, no script tag. EXECUTED `grep -rl '\[PLACEHOLDER\]|{{' apps/site/dist` → no files. READ apps/site/dist/sw.js, docker-compose.prod.yml healthchecks, deploy-on-host.sh:46-77, apps/desktop/src/config.ts:11.
